name: Adolion Narrator
text:
You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

name: Max Nightriver
text: I go to Father's study at once.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."

name: Javon
text: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I keep my own counsel.

name: Javon
text:
"Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"

name: Max Nightriver
text: I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"

name: Shiya
text:
Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*

name: Max Nightriver
text: I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"

name: Natalia
text:
The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."

name: Natalia
text:
Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."

name: Max Nightriver
text: "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."

name: Natalia
text:
Natalia's expression doesn't change, but the frost creeping across the arms of her chair thickens. She remains perfectly still for a heartbeat, then speaks in a voice so quiet it barely carries across the small space between them. "You'll fight a traitor in the lists." The words are flat, devoid of surprise. "How perfectly Father."
*She leans forward, her green eyes sharp as emerald glass.*
"Centuries ago, before the Lich Queen was slain, she had a servant—the Witch King. When she fell, he was not destroyed, only sealed away by the magic of the first Great Houses. The seal requires Nightriver blood to remain. You, me, Welden—we each carry a part of that lock in our very veins." She lets that settle, her voice dropping even lower. "If the line ends, he wakes. If the blood thins, he stirs. Father is obsessed with our marriages because he's not arranging alliances—he's securing the lock. Kippon Bertoanal isn't just a husband to me; he's the next link in a chain that keeps a monster from returning to Sebela."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I go back down to Father's study. "Fine. I'll stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon. Tell the court."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I nod once and leave him to his watch. In the corridor I keep my ears open for whatever the servants are whispering about the duel.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The corridor is dimly lit by wall sconces, their flames flickering in the drafts. The sound of a heavy door closing echoes from somewhere below stairs. Two maids hurry past in silence, their heads bent and shoulders tense, too hurried to notice Max Nightriver.
A soft voice catches from an alcove up ahead—whispers, urgent and low. "...in the lists? Against a general?" A maid's voice, trembling. "The boy won't survive. He'll be slaughtered."
"Hush," comes Shiya's sharp rebuke, her tone cutting through the air like a blade. "Not for your ears, and not for mine. Move on, or I'll have you scrubbing the wine cellars."

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The maids scatter like startled birds, their footsteps pattering quickly down the hall until the sound fades into nothing. The alcove stands empty now, save for a lingering scent of incense and the cold draft that whistles through the corridor's gaps.
Shiya has vanished, her sharp footsteps silent as she disappears into the shadows of the servants' stairwell. Only the flickering torchlight remains, casting long, dancing shadows against the stone walls. The estate is quiet once more, but it's the silence of bated breath, like the house itself is waiting for what comes next.

name: Max Nightriver
text: I find Shiya in the alcove. "The maids say I'll be slaughtered. Do you agree?"

name: Shiya
text:
Shiya stops mid-turn, her red eyes locking onto Max Nightriver with startled precision. For a heartbeat her composure falters, and her grip tightens on the tray she carries. Then her chin lifts, haughty as ever. "The maids say the sun is too bright and the rain too wet," she snaps. "They speak for their mouths, not their minds."
*She steps closer, and for a moment her arrogance drops, leaving something raw and sharp beneath.*
"Do I agree?" Her voice softens, nearly a whisper. "I agree that you are a fool. But then again," her lips curve into a mocking smile, "I suppose that's why I'm paid to make sure fools don't kill themselves."

name: Max Nightriver
text: Three days pass in drills and bad sleep. On the morning of the trial I walk out into the lists before the whole court and face General Leevon.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The lists are a bowl of packed earth surrounded by a high stone wall. The banners of the Great Houses snap in the wind, their colors vivid against the grey sky. At the head of the court sits King Alexander, his face a mask of royal indifference, while beside him stands a Herald in gold and crimson.
The crowd is a sea of murmur and expectation. Nobles whisper behind silk fans, and knights in polished plate watch with narrow eyes. The air tastes of dust and anticipation, sharp as a whetted edge.
General Leevon enters from the opposing gate. He is a mountain of a man in black plate, his greyed hair cropped short, his weathered face scarred and grim. His dragon-bone lance is a pale, terrible thing in his grip, and his eyes are chips of ice. He doesn't look at the court or the King. He looks only at you, and his smile is slow and predatory.
The Herald's voice rings out: "Max Nightriver, Second for House Nightriver! General Polis Leevon, Accused of Treason! The Trial by Combat commences now. Boher guide the worthy."
The two of you stand a hundred feet apart, steel and bone and magic, while the court holds its breath.

name: Adolion Narrator
text: Evening settles over the estate. Lamps are lit along the gallery, and somewhere below, the door of Lord Javon's study opens and closes.

name: Adolion Narrator
text: A herald's voice rolls over the packed dueling ground. "By the King's law, General Polis Leevon, accused of treason, claims the Trial by Combat. Let the Crown's second step forward."

name: Max Nightriver
text: I step forward, then raise my hand before the first pass. "Before we fight: I show the court the venom on his lance."

name: Merryn
text:
Merryn rises from her seat in the royal gallery, white high-collared priestess robes rustling as she stands. Her horse ears prick forward, alert, and her red eyes flash with sudden intensity.
"Herald! Halt the trial," she calls, her voice clear and commanding enough to cut through the rising murmur of the court. She steps to the edge of the gallery, gold cross pendant catching the light as she points a slender finger toward General Leevon's lance. "As High Saintess, I must demand an examination of the weapon before any blow is struck."
*The General's grip on the dragon-bone lance tightens, his weathered face hardening as the court falls into a shocked silence.*

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
The Herald freezes, his hand still raised to call the first pass, and the royal guards step forward to block the path between the combatants. King Alexander leans forward in his throne, brown eyes narrowing as he regards the High Saintess's interruption with slow, calculated interest.
General Leevon stands like a statue in black plate, the dragon-bone lance held level across his chest. His knuckles are white where they grip the weapon, and the muscle in his scarred jaw twitches. The crowd presses against the wall, nobles leaning over the parapets, their whispers rising into a roar of speculation as Merryn's demand hangs in the air.

name: Max Nightriver
text: When Leevon refuses to yield the lance, I draw shadow around me and meet his charge. I aim for the haft, not the man, and break the poisoned lance in front of the King.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
General Leevon does not yield. His eyes flare with lightning as he lowers his lance and spurs his horse into a thunderous charge, dragon-bone tip pointed directly at Max Nightriver's chest. The court screams as the massive warrior gallops forward, the earth shaking beneath hooves, the lance already beginning to glow with gathering electricity.
Shadow coils around Max Nightriver like a living cloak, dark and viscous as ink, and for a heartbeat the crowd goes silent at the unnatural sight. As the General closes the distance—twenty feet, ten, a final lunging strike—Max Nightriver moves. The blow does not fall on flesh, but on the haft of the lance itself, and there is a sound like a falling mountain: the dragon-bone weapon shatters with a violent crack that echoes across the lists.
Splinters fly in a deadly arc, and the lance-tip clatters to the dirt. In the moment of impact, a foul-smelling liquid—dark, viscous, and smelling of copper and rot—sprays across the packed earth from the broken bone. The crowd gasps and recoils, the stench of poison thick enough to taste. General Leevon rears in his saddle, his horse neighing in protest, his weapon reduced to a useless stump.

name: Merryn
text:
Merryn is already on her feet, her red eyes wide as she leans over the gallery's edge. The moment the poison sprays across the dirt, she turns to King Alexander with urgent authority.
"Your Majesty!" she calls out, her voice ringing across the silent lists. "The poison is revealed! General Leevon has violated the sanctity of this Trial by Combat by envenoming his weapon!" She points down at the shattered dragon-bone, the dark viscous liquid seeping into the earth like an ink stain. "I demand the lance be gathered and examined by the Church immediately, before the court!"

name: Ronan
text:
Ronan steps forward from the Nightriver retinue, his boots crunching on the packed earth as he advances toward the edge of the lists. His hand rests on the pommel of his rapier, knuckles white, eyes locked on the shattered remnants of the dragon-bone lance and the venom seeping across the ground. He does not draw his blade—not yet—but his posture is coiled and ready, muscles tense beneath his leather armor.
His gaze flickers briefly to Max Nightriver, checking for wounds, before returning to the still-mounted General Leevon. When the High Saintess demands the examination, Ronan's jaw sets. He stays close, watchful, his presence a silent declaration that the heir is not alone. If the General makes a move, if a guard steps too close, Ronan will be there in a heartbeat. He waits, motionless as a statue, for the King's word.

name: Max Nightriver
text: I keep my shadow up and look to the King for his judgment.

name: Adolion Narrator
text:
King Alexander stands slowly from his throne, his dark brown eyes fixed on the venom seeping into the dirt of the lists. He says nothing for a long moment, his expression unreadable. The silence stretches, broken only by the distant murmur of the crowd and the sound of the wind whipping the banners.
"You are right, High Saintess," the King says finally, his voice carrying across the dueling ground. "The sanctification of a Trial by Combat is absolute. A weapon must be clean. General Leevon—" He looks directly at the accused, who still sits mounted and rigid on his horse. "—you will yield the shattered lance. The Church shall examine it now. If poison is confirmed, this trial is voided by your own hand, and you will answer for this crime in a different manner."
Two royal guards advance to the lists, their hands resting on their sword hilts as they move to secure the shattered weapon and ensure the General does not resist.

name: Adolion Narrator
text: Somewhere below, a servants' door that should have been barred for the night clicks softly shut.

name: Merryn
text:
"The Radiant's blessings on you all," Merryn says softly, her voice carrying a note of solemn relief as she returns to her seat in the royal gallery. Her horse ears flatten against her white hair, and she watches the royal guards with an unblinking, intense gaze. "May the Truth guide the Church's hand."
*Her gold cross pendant catches the light as she settles back into her place, but her posture remains rigid, alert. Her red eyes don't leave the shattered remnants of the dragon-bone lance as the guards move to secure it for examination. The High Saintess has seen enough for today; now comes the waiting.*
